title: Nelsonic Labs private connectivity scouting call
summary: Initial scoping call to understand Nelsonic's requirements for a private Redwood deployment. Key topics: VPC peering vs. PrivateLink/private endpoints, multi-region constraints, audit/KMS needs, expected qps and latency SLOs, and proof-of-concept criteria. Customer leaned toward a private VPC deployment with private endpoints in two regions but has concerns about egress IPs, KMS integration, and on-prem traffic routing.
topics: VPC peering vs PrivateLink (AWS) and equivalents on other clouds
Egress IP management and IP whitelisting
action_items: Owen Park: Share draft network diagram and example terraform for PrivateLink + endpoint services; due 2026-03-03
Maya Chen: Send Nelsonic pricing summary for Dedicated vs Private (1yr and 3yr) and pilot credits; due 2026-03-02
Priya Raman: Provide current egress IP range and preferred regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1); due 2026-03-04
Lena Ko: Confirm KMS provider (AWS KMS) requirements and whether HSM-backed keys required; due 2026-03-05
next_steps: Schedule technical deep dive with networking team (SE-led) next week
Run short smoke benchmark during pilot: 100 qps sustained for 10 minutes across two regions
Exchange security questionnaire and SOC2 artifacts via shared drive link
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-27 16:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Owen Park (Redwood); Priya Raman, Diego Alvarez, Lena Ko (Nelsonic)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Owen Park, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:07] Priya: Hi Maya, thanks. Priya here. We have Diego and Lena on as well. Excited to get into private connectivity options.
[00:13] Owen: Hey, nice to meet you all. Quick agenda — want to understand your topology, constraints, and then walk through our private options: VPC peering, private endpoints/privatelink, and hybrid on-prem connectivity.
[00:25] Diego: Sounds good. We already did a bit of homework on Redwood's hosted offering — looks great — but for compliance reasons we need the private deployment.
[00:33] Maya: Totally, that's what we hear a lot. Can you sketch your high-level infra and the exact blockers pushing you to private?
[00:40] Priya: Sure. We're a regulated fintech, so data must remain in our VPCs and we need control over egress IPs. Our app runs in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 primarily, some on-prem traffic for legacy systems. We want the inference traffic to stay over private links — basically no public internet egress.
[00:56] Lena: And we need KMS keys managed by us. We may require HSM-backed keys for certain workloads. Audit logs retention is a requirement (7 years for specific flows).
[01:05] Owen: Ok good detail. On the KMS side, we support AWS KMS integrations for Private deployments; we also support bringing-your-own-key with rotated keys. HSM-backed KMS is something we've integrated with customers before but there are a few integration steps.
[01:18] Maya: Can you clarify the network path you envision — are you thinking VPC peering to Redwood's VPCs, or using PrivateLink / endpoint services?
[01:25] Priya: We're evaluating both. Peering seems simpler but we've seen issues with transitive routing and cross-account management. PrivateLink feels more controlled but we need to understand cross-region availability and throughput limits.
[01:37] Owen: Both are viable. Quick pros/cons: peering is straightforward high-bandwidth MM but you need route management and it can be messy across multiple accounts/regions. PrivateLink gives per-endpoint control and enforced private traffic — also better for IP whitelisting. Downside: per-region endpoint setup; on AWS theres NLBs behind the endpoint with potential throughput configs.
[01:58] Diego: Right, throughput matters. Our expected traffic for the pilot is about 100 qps with 5–15 token responses typically; production could jump to 1k qps eventually. Latency SLO is 150ms p95 for user-facing flows. Can Redwood meet that inside private?
[02:16] Owen: Short answer — yes depending on model and hosting mode. For private deployments we run colocated inference clusters; p95 will depend on batching config, model size, and distance to region. For the pilot we can tune batching to favor latency. We can also route traffic to a lower-latency variant.
[02:33] Maya: Also important — caching/KV cache behavior when using private endpoints. If you have warm caches close to your traffic region we can keep latencies low.
[02:41] Priya: About egress IPs — we need static egress IP addresses per region so our vendor APIs can whitelist. How is egress handled when we use PrivateLink vs peering?
[02:52] Owen: With peering, traffic stays in the VPCs and egress is controlled by your nat/gateway settings so you can ensure fixed IPs. For PrivateLink, the endpoint inside your VPC connects to our service; egress from Redwood's side may originate from Redwood-managed IPs. We offer options: dedicated egress IP pools for Dedicated/Private customers, or you can route via our transit gateway in specific setups to give predictable egress. We'll need to map your whitelist needs.
[03:20] Lena: So there's a potential for Redwood IPs to show up on vendor logs unless we peer and force all egress through our own NAT?
[03:26] Owen: Correct, but we can set up per-customer egress addresses in many cases. We'll share the doc with the egress options matrix.
[03:33] Diego: Region availability — you mentioned eu-west-1 is fine. Do you support PrivateLink in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 concurrently?
[03:41] Owen: Yes, we maintain endpoint services in multiple regions; the caveat is that for private endpoints you need one endpoint per region. Cross-region traffic will traverse our internal backbone or your peering arrangement — that can add latency. For strict data residency you can pin inference to region-local model replicas.
[04:00] Priya: Pinning per region is important — certain datasets can't leave EU. Can we enforce policies per model to keep data in eu-west-1?
[04:08] Owen: Absolutely. We have deployment policies that let customers pin model versions to regions, and routing rules to prevent cross-region fallbacks unless explicitly allowed.
[04:16] Maya: What's the onboarding timeline for Private? For example, if we sign a pilot agreement, how soon can we have endpoints in both regions?
[04:23] Owen: Typical timeline: 2–3 weeks for initial network setup and validating peering or PrivateLink, then 1 week to spin up model replicas and run smoke tests. If you need HSM KMS integration that can add another ~1–2 weeks depending on your KMS admin availability.
[04:41] Priya: That aligns with our internal schedule. One risk: our on-prem batch workers need to call the inference endpoint across a private VPN. Does Redwood support VPN peering or SD-WAN connectors?
[04:53] Owen: Yes, for Private deployments we support VPN tunnels and direct connect style setups. Often customers use a transit gateway or VPN into the VPC that holds the private endpoints. We'll coordinate with your network team on BGP and route tables.
[05:06] Diego: About RBAC and audit logs — we need token-level audit logs and SSO integration (SAML). Is that available in Private?
[05:14] Maya: Yes, SSO/SAML is supported; for Private we can federate into your IdP and we maintain token-level request logs which can be pushed to your log aggregator or stored for X days. For the specific retention you mentioned (7 years), that's more of an enterprise add-on — we'll capture the requirement and include it in the security pack.
[05:34] Lena: We'll want to see sample audit artifacts and SOC2 report.
[05:37] Maya: We'll share SOC2 and typical audit artifacts. Expect to exchange an NDA if needed.
[05:43] Priya: Can we talk about model versions and rollouts — if you do a canary, does traffic ever go out of region?
[05:50] Owen: By default rollouts respect your routing policies. We can configure canary routes within the same region. Cross-region canaries are only done if you opt-in; otherwise fallbacks stay local.
[06:02] Priya: Ok good. One more: encryption in transit — does Redwood terminate TLS inside our VPC or at their NLB? We need end-to-end control unless we accept our certs being offloaded.
[06:13] Owen: We support mTLS to the endpoint and you can present your TLS certs on the endpoint in a PrivateLink setup. If you need end-to-end crypto using your certs we can do that.
[06:24] Diego: For the pilot benchmarks — we want a reproducible script. Can Redwood provide a loadgen config that hits private endpoints and measures p50/p95 and token throughput?
[06:33] Owen: Yes, we'll provide a JMeter/Locust example plus our recommended prompt set. We'll also provide a small harness to measure token costs and latencies.
[06:42] Priya: Great. About cost — how different is Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private-managed in terms of pricing? We want both economic predictability and isolation.
[06:52] Maya: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools you control, good for predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale. Private adds a private control plane and network isolation; price delta depends on capacity commitment and support SLAs. I'll send a side-by-side pricing with sample compute configs.
[07:08] Diego: Any competitors with stronger on-prem story? We looked at a few.
[07:12] Maya: Some self-hosted vendors tout on-prem but they often lack the operational automation. Redwood focuses on unified ops across hosted/dedicated/private — we run the runtime but integrate into your network.
[07:24] Priya: Ok that's helpful.
[07:26] Speaker 6: (inaudible)
[07:29] Owen: I'll circle back with a networking diagram. Quick question for you Priya — do you need inbound IP ranges for our side or will you accept an accept-list for the endpoint service?
[07:38] Priya: We prefer to control inbound via our own SGs and accept-list Redwood's endpoint DNS names, but for vendor whitelisting we need static egress IPs to provide to third-party vendors.
[07:49] Owen: Noted. We'll provide the egress IP options and which ones require Dedicated.
[07:55] Maya: Wrapping up — key asks from our side: Nelsonic to send exact region list and egress IP needs; Redwood to send network diagram, terraform snippets for PrivateLink, and SOC2 artifacts.
[08:06] Priya: Yep we'll share a sheet with regions and expected qps per region.
[08:11] Diego: Timeline — we'll aim to review your materials by March 9 and schedule the deep dive the week after.
[08:17] Maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll send notes and next steps.
[08:21] Lena: Thanks, bye.

Meeting end. Notes: occasional mis-attributions present, transcription may have minor word swaps (e.g., "privatelink" vs "PrivateLink"). Shared artifacts: link to drive/nelsonic-onboarding (redacted placeholder), draft network diagram (to be added).
